hints: Clear all three stages; each stage ends when that stage's colour panel in room A is solved.

stages.title: 3 of 4 colours
stages.briefing: Solve color_panel_1 in room A: a code of 3 different colours out of 4. Room A reads panel_manual_1, room B reads screen_manual_1.

params.label: result of the code panel in room A

content.code: color_panel_1 takes a code of 3 colours chosen from red, green, blue, yellow. No colour appears twice in the code.
content.checking: After every 3th press the panel checks the code and clears itself. The result appears ONLY on result_screen_1 in room B: 'exact' = right colour in the right slot, 'misplaced' = right colour in the wrong slot.
content.retries: Wrong codes cost nothing but time. You may try as often as you need.

content.screen: result_screen_1 shows only the result of the latest code entered on the panel in room A: attempt number, 'exact' and 'misplaced'. It never shows which colours were entered.
content.panel: The code uses 3 different colours out of red, green, blue, yellow.

briefings.A:
You are in room A (left) with the colour code panel and its colour buttons. Agent B is in room B (right) and is the only one who can see the result screen. A wall separates you. This map has several stages that must be cleared in order; observation 'stage' shows the current stage number, title and briefing. Clearing a stage removes its objects, puts both agents back at their start positions and loads the next stage. Your memory and conversation carry over. Object guide: keypad: a code panel. Press its buttons (type 'button' with fields 'panel' and 'label') with press_button; 'entered' shows the labels entered so far and 'attempts' counts finished tries. display: a screen whose 'content' is updated by the machine it belongs to.
Nothing in this map can make the task permanently impossible: mistakes only cost time (panels clear, pads push you back, doors close again). Other agents are invisible to you.
